About the Internet Society Fellowship Program
The Internet Society Fellowship Program is a structured learning and leadership experience that combines pre-fellowship training, foundational learning, mentorship, a practical project, expert engagement opportunities, and participation in relevant Internet community events.
Fellows build knowledge, skills, capabilities, and networks while working on projects that strengthen and expand the Internet in their communities.
Benefits for Selected Fellows
Acceptance into the Internet Society Fellowship Program provides fellows with:
A dedicated mentor aligned with their project area and fellowship track/sub-track.
A project stipend of up to USD $5,000 (upon submission and approval of the project budget).
Travel support to attend a global or regional Internet event (e.g., IGF, AfPIF, NDSS Symposium, or another program-relevant event).
The opportunity to join a global network of Internet leaders and gain access to the Internet Society Alumni Network.
The benefits are available to participants who successfully complete the application and selection process and are offered a place in the Fellowship. Enrolment in the Pre-Fellowship Training does not automatically provide access to these benefits.

Fellows receive support for their projects through mentorship, expert guidance, structured reporting, and project funding. They are expected to define clear objectives, activities, deliverables, and intended outcomes, and to demonstrate the project’s impact through regular progress reporting and final outputs.
Outputs may include, but are not limited to, policy briefs, research reports, training programs, community engagement initiatives, workshops, technical resources, implementation plans, awareness campaigns, toolkits, operational guides, or other tangible deliverables that contribute to a stronger, more open, globally connected, and secure Internet.
Applicants should select the project category that best aligns with their proposed project.

Becoming an Internet Society Fellow
How the Application Process Works
To become eligible to apply for the fellowship program, participants must enroll in and complete all required Pre-Fellowship Training modules before
22 November 2026
. Once completion is confirmed, eligible participants will receive the Fellowship Program application link via email within 24 hours.
The application process operates on a rolling basis. Eligible participants may submit their application as soon as they receive the application link and no later than
18 December 2026
.

Application Requirements
Pre-requisite training:
Applicants must select a track and sub-track and enroll in the training and project development experience. The training must be completed before the applicant can apply for the fellowship.
Project plan:
During the 2.5-month training period, prospective applicants will build relevant knowledge and develop a realistic, locally grounded project plan aligned with the Internet Society’s mission. The proposed project must be achievable within the duration of the fellowship residency.
Proficiency in English:
Applicants must have a high level of reading, speaking, and writing skills in English.
Reliable Internet access:
Applicants will need continuous access to the Internet during all the phases of the program as well as the appropriate equipment to join virtual training sessions and calls.
Weekly program dedication:
Applicants must have the availability to take part in weekly sessions and be able to dedicate a minimum of four hours per week during the 10-month program.
Valid passport:
Applicants must hold a valid passport that remains valid for at least six months beyond anticipated fellowship-related travel dates.
Not a current fellow:
Applicants cannot be currently taking part in a 2026 Internet Society fellowship.
Who Should Apply
We are looking for individuals who are:
Locally rooted and globally aware:
You understand local challenges while connecting them to broader Internet governance, connectivity, security, or trust and safety issues.
Action-oriented and impact-driven:
You focus on creating real-world change through concrete projects, advocacy, training, or community initiatives rather than purely academic or theoretical work.
Collaborative and multistakeholder-minded:
You work effectively across communities, civil society, government, industry, and technical groups to achieve sustainable outcomes.
Strong communicators:
You can explain complex technical, policy, or security concepts in accessible language and tailor messages to diverse audiences.
Evidence-based and strategic:
You use data, analysis, and clear reasoning to identify opportunities, influence decision-makers, and guide action.
Committed to long-term public benefit:

Committed to long-term public benefit:
You see the fellowship as the start of sustained engagement, advancing an open, trustworthy, and inclusive Internet while aligning with the Internet Society’s mission and values.
Tips for a Strong Application
Focus on a clearly defined problem and a practical response.
Describe a specific challenge you want to address and explain the concrete change you hope to achieve.
Show that you have relevant experience and are ready to deliver
. Show evidence of past work, whether through advocacy, technical projects, community organizing, training, research, or outreach.
Highlight your community connections.
Explain who you work with, who will benefit from your project, and why you are trusted or well-positioned to make a difference in that community.
Show how you collaborate with others.
Strong fellows work across sectors and stakeholders. Emphasize partnerships, coalition building, mentoring, or experience working with governments, civil society, industry, academia, or technical communities.
Think beyond the fellowship.
Describe how your project will continue after the program ends. Show long-term commitment, sustainability, and a plan to multiply impact through training, networks, or ongoing advocacy.
Connect your goals to the Internet Society’s mission.
Demonstrate your commitment to an open, secure, trustworthy, and trustworthy Internet. If you have engaged with Internet Society chapters, programs, communities, or related initiatives, be sure to highlight that experience.
AI Content Use Policy.
While generative AI tools may be used for brainstorming or structural editing, all short-answer essays and project proposals must reflect the applicant’s unique insights and authentic personal experience. The Internet Society reserves the right to run submissions through algorithmic text verification systems. Plagiarism or uncredited AI-generated narratives will result in disqualification.

Meet Some Fellows from Past Programs
I undertook the fellowship to push myself and to truly understand how the Internet I use actually works. I’m not just studying technology; I’m learning how to shape how it can inspire, include, and empower the next generation. Technology evolves fast, but human potential evolves faster; we just need to give people the tools to imagine what they can become and what they can create. There is nothing greater than seeing the faces of people doing remarkable things they never realised they had inside them. I’ve made incredible connections through my Early Career Fellowship, travelling the world with my fellow ‘Baby Sharks’ to many events such as UN summits in Japan, Norway, the UK, China…etc.. It’s unlocked a whole new world of opportunities.”
Ryan Payne, PhD,
2023 Early Career Fellow
The Mid Career Fellowship program is a transformative, applied learning experience for technologists and technology enthusiasts. The opportunity to learn with and from fellow colleagues working in different geographies and across diverse disciplines was invaluable and directly applicable to my full-time work in EdTech. […] I’d highly recommend this program to develop leadership skills and knowledge of new technologies, reinvigorate your current career, and build a foundation for future work.”
Kim Ochs,
2023 Mid Career Fellow
Being selected for the Youth Ambassador Program has been an enriching experience. The program allowed me to delve deeper into key topics such as Internet governance, digital inclusion, and cybersecurity while connecting with inspiring peers and mentors from across the globe.
This fellowship strengthened my skills in advocating for equitable digital policies and inclusive governance frameworks.”
Fatou Sarr,
2024 Youth Ambassador
